hook_text: 3/8 plus 2/8. Is it 5/16 or 5/8? One picture settles it.
clip_script: A bakery in Paarl. 3/8 of a bag of flour this morning, 2/8 this afternoon. Draw the bag in 8 pieces. Shade 3, then 2 more. 5 pieces out of 8. 5/8. Not 5/16: the bag did not grow more cuts. Add the tops, keep the bottom. Now the hike in the Drakensberg: 2 and 3/8 km plus 1 and 2/8 km. Wholes: 3. Pieces: 5/8. 3 and 5/8 km. And taking away: 3 and 1/4 minus 1 and 3/4. Not enough quarters, so break a whole: 2 and 5/4. Now 1 and 2/4. Same pieces, add the tops, and swap wholes for pieces when you need to.
visual_style: A flour bag drawn as a bar of 8 parts shading in, then a hiking trail with whole kilometres and eighths marked.
mood: Warm and homely, like baking with a patient grandparent.
pacing: The 5/16 trap first, the picture proof, then mixed numbers and the break-a-whole twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out 2 and 1/3 minus 1 and 2/3.
